summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and diabetes was admitted with bright red blood per rectum and midsternal chest pain. The rectal bleeding had resolved by the time of admission, and no active source was identified, though guaiac testing was positive. His chest pain was persistent and not relieved by nitroglycerin, but cardiac enzymes showed no significant rise and ECG changes were chronic. The pain improved after hemodialysis and resolved by discharge. The patient remained hemodynamically stable, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with cardiology and gastroenterology.
